detail.longDescription: arXiv:2611.33172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the Tragedy of the Commons (ToC) problem, which commonly arises in heterogeneous distributed resource allocation, in which selfish users are independently interested in optimizing their own utility. Such self-interested decision-making in decentralized settings often results in inefficient resource utilization because users prefer high-capacity resources, leading to their overutilization. We cast the problem into a non-cooperative game and derive closed-form characterizations of both the distributed Nash equilibrium (NE) and the socially optimal allocation. In view of these closed-form expressions, we establish the structural conditions under which the ToC arises, and derive an exact expression for the Price of Anarchy (PoA). We further prove that the PoA can become arbitrarily large (unbounded) under suitable traffic conditions. Motivated by these observations, we propose a penalty-based incentive mechanism that discourages the use of overloaded servers while preserving decentralized decision-making. We analyze the resulting equilibrium load redistribution and establish conditions under which the proposed mechanism reduces the overall system cost and improves equilibrium efficiency.
